speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You presented with gait and limb ataxia; to begin our investigation, do you have a specific history of head trauma, alcohol use disorder, or exposure to heavy metals like mercury or arsenic?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: The patient describes a recent onset of gait instability and limb clumsiness, specifically noting symptoms are worse on the right side. Have you noticed any changes in your handwriting, vision, or the ability to swallow?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: PML (Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy).

Your history of Crohn's disease and specifically your use of natalizumab for a year puts you at high risk for this opportunistic infection of the central nervous system. We need to confirm this immediately; I am ordering an MRI of your brain and a test for John Cunningham (JC) virus in your spinal fluid.
